 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Lewis Hamilton has no patience for former drivers who trash talk the new generation of racing stars. The seven-time champion said he sees too much negativity aimed at young drivers who are just trying to survive the pressure. He made his feelings clear during a press moment in Sao Paulo, where he defended the kids taking over the grid. Motorsport.com reports that "talking smack" regarding the series' young stars drew criticism from Hamilton targeting older racers.
 Last week in Sao Paulo, the 41-year-old Ferrari driver completed his 400th grand prix start. He said he was proud to see new people coming through the ranks. He noted that many ex-drivers just talk smack about young people all the time. Hamilton said those critics showed "no empathy" even though they faced similar struggles. He added that he always wanted to make sure he would not be that type of driver.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Hard Reality of the Pinnacle
 Hamilton knows the grind better than anyone. He called the sport the hardest platform to do well in. He said it is so easy to make mistakes at this level. He acknowledged the respect due to young drivers who repeatedly rise and continue pushing forward. These kids face massive challenges just to arrive and keep their heads up. The criticism from the old guard ignores the sheer difficulty of the job.
 Mercedes technical director James Allison said the team's recent defeats have taken a mental toll. He admitted it is hard to think about the sport and its fans while the team struggles in the trenches. Allison said he finds it very hard to lift himself out of the melee they are in. His thoughts focus solely on friends and team-mates who endured the last seasons of underperformance. That experience brought self-doubt and, at the extreme, self-loathing, as he described.
 Young Stars Are Delivering Results
 In only his second season, Kimi Antonelli secured the title after winning nine grands prix. The Italian driver has 16 podiums to his name. At just 22 years old, Red Bull's Isack Hadjar has achieved three podium finishes during his second season. These numbers prove the young drivers are ready for the spotlight.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Antonelli is signed to Mercedes until the end of 2027. Hadjar's deal with Red Bull expires at the end of 2027. Hamilton himself is locked in with Ferrari until 2027. Photo: Joe Portlock / Getty Images – Lewis Hamilton at Ferrari.
